title: The Scientific Revolution
note: Harari argues that modern science began when Europeans admitted ignorance and joined research to empire and capital, driving growth and, with the Industrial Revolution, a new world of state and market. The dates and inventions are empirical; the causal loop and his claims about family and community are his interpretation.

read.title: Ignorance, empire and growth
text: Harari argues that the Scientific Revolution, usually dated from 1543 when Copernicus and Vesalius published their books, rested on a change of attitude. Earlier cultures, he says, tended to believe their sacred texts already contained all the knowledge that mattered. Europeans from about 1500 began saying openly that they did not know, and set out to find out. Combined with observation and mathematics, this produced new power.

He then links science to empire and capital. Explorers and conquerors collected plants, maps and customs, and rulers paid for research that promised military and economic advantage. Meanwhile capitalism, in Harari's description, depends on credit, meaning trust in future growth, and on reinvesting profits. The loop of science, empire and capital drove expansion. This is his causal story, and historians disagree about how much weight each part deserves.

The Industrial Revolution is easier to date: it began in Great Britain around 1760 in textiles, with steam engines by Newcomen and Watt and coal replacing wood. Harari emphasizes energy conversion, the ability to turn heat into motion. He also argues that the state and the market took over many tasks of family and community. Others dispute how complete that change was, since families and communities still do much of the work of care.
Both threads show the book's pattern. The dates are checkable. The big explanation is Harari's argument.

q.q: What change of attitude does Harari credit for modern science?
o: Admitting what people did not know

q.q: Where did the Industrial Revolution begin?
Which is presented as Harari's interpretation rather than a date?
o: The state and market took over from family and community
